title: Web console epic P0: research spike — persistent headless orchestrator session over the existing claude login
description:
EPIC: "Agentic OS web console" — a local, browser-based front-end so a NON-TECHNICAL user (cannot/won't use the terminal) can drive this framework with buttons + plain chat, at NO extra cost (reuses the existing Claude account/login they already have), with NOTHING new to install (simple HTML served by the framework's own zero-dep Node server). The browser chat is a window into a PERSISTENT live orchestrator session (one per browser tab) that behaves exactly like the main Claude Code thread: reads state/, spawns developer/reviewer/researcher subagents, moves tickets. Scope locked with the human: local-only single-user (127.0.0.1, reuse board hardening); EXTEND the existing task-board server (src/task-board.js); skill buttons RUN immediately on click.

THIS TICKET (P0) is a read-only RESEARCH SPIKE that de-risks the one true unknown before any bridge code is written: HOW to hold a persistent, streaming orchestrator session driven from a local web server, reusing the user's existing `claude` CLI login (NO API key, NO new billing relationship). The deliverable is a design note + a reusable Agent Skill, NOT production code.

Questions to answer with cited sources (use the researcher subagent / claude-code-guide; prefer official Claude Code + Agent SDK docs):
1. Persistent streaming session mechanics: can `claude` run in a long-lived process accepting MULTIPLE user turns over stdin and emitting assistant/tool events over stdout? Confirm the exact flags (e.g. --input-format stream-json / --output-format stream-json / --print / --resume / --session-id / --continue), the stdin message envelope shape, and the stdout event schema (assistant text deltas, tool_use / tool_result events, subagent/Task spawn signals, turn-complete markers, errors).
2. Auth/cost: confirm that a spawned `claude` process reuses the EXISTING interactive login (subscription) with no API key and no separate per-token bill — and document any case where it would fall back to an API key (must be avoidable). This is a HARD epic constraint.
3. Session continuity: how to keep conversation memory across user turns within one tab (single long-lived process vs --resume/--session-id reattach). Document the chosen continuity model and its failure/restart behavior.
4. Alternative compared & rejected-or-deferred: the Claude Agent SDK in-process. State explicitly why the CLI-spawn path wins for the no-extra-cost + nothing-to-install constraints (or, if the SDK can also reuse the subscription login with no API key, capture that and let the bridge ticket choose).
5. Working-directory + concurrency: confirm the spawned session can run with cwd = the user's project (so it picks up CLAUDE.md, .claude/, state/) and note the one-orchestrator-at-a-time hazard (web session + a separate Claude Code session both writing state/).
6. Streaming transport to the browser: SSE vs WebSocket for relaying the event stream from the Node server to the page — recommend one for a zero-dep Node http server.

Deliverables: (a) a design note committed under tasks/ (e.g. tasks/TASK-050.research.md) capturing answers 1-6 with citations and a concrete recommended bridge architecture (process model, message framing, event mapping, transport); (b) a reusable Agent Skill under .claude/skills/<stack-name>/ ONLY if a genuinely new stack/tool is involved (per the researcher's standing rule) — e.g. a "claude-headless" skill documenting the streaming-session invocation; (c) an explicit go/no-go on the CLI-spawn bridge with any blockers surfaced.

This is a spike: no app code, no new tests beyond what a skill needs. Verified via UAT (human reads the design note + go/no-go).
acceptance_criteria: A design note is committed (tasks/TASK-050.research.md) answering all six research questions with citations to official Claude Code / Agent SDK documentation, and ending in a concrete recommended bridge architecture: process model (single long-lived `claude` vs per-turn --resume), stdin message framing, stdout event-to-UI mapping (text deltas, tool_use/tool_result, subagent spawns, turn-complete, errors), and the browser transport choice (SSE vs WebSocket) with rationale.

The note CONFIRMS, with a citation, that the spawned `claude` session reuses the user's existing interactive login (subscription) requiring NO API key and creating NO separate per-token bill, and documents how to ensure the no-API-key path (and any fallback to avoid). If this cannot be confirmed, the note says so explicitly and the spike returns NO-GO with the reason.

The note states the session-continuity model (how conversation memory survives across user turns within one tab) and the restart/failure behavior, plus the one-orchestrator-at-a-time concurrency hazard and a recommended mitigation.
The Agent-SDK-in-process alternative is compared and explicitly rejected-or-deferred for THIS epic with reasons grounded in the no-extra-cost + nothing-to-install constraints.

If a genuinely new stack/tool is involved, a reusable Agent Skill is created under .claude/skills/ documenting the streaming-session invocation (frontmatter description states WHEN to load it); if not, the note explains why no skill was warranted.
A clear GO or NO-GO recommendation for the CLI-spawn bridge is recorded, with any blockers enumerated, so TASK-051 can start (or be re-scoped) without further research.

comments.body:
UAT (uat-only spike) — verified by Orchestrator at the human's standing 'proceed until the end' request; deliverables read on disk. Overall: PASS (6/6).
1. AC1 design note answers all six Qs + concrete bridge architecture (process model, stdin framing, stdout→UI event map, SSE transport) — expect: note with §1-6 + ## Recommended Bridge Architecture; observed: tasks/TASK-050.research.md has all sections (verified headings). PASS.
2. AC2 no-API-key/subscription confirmed with citation + the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY-precedence guard documented — expect: explicit auth/cost section; observed: §2 cites authentication docs + the June-15-2026 Agent-SDK-credit split (no new key, distinct credit bucket). PASS.
3. AC3 continuity model + restart behavior + one-orchestrator concurrency hazard — expect: documented; observed: §3 (long-lived process, --resume recovery) + §5 (hazard + mitigation). PASS.
4. AC4 Agent-SDK alternative compared & rejected on the cost/install constraints — expect: short comparison; observed: §4 rejects in-process SDK (needs API key / duplicates wiring). PASS.
5. AC5 reusable skill created — expect: .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with WHEN-to-load frontmatter; observed: .claude/skills/claude-headless/SKILL.md (loaded this session, triggers documented). PASS.
6. AC6 explicit GO/NO-GO with blockers — expect: verdict; observed: ## Go / No-Go = GO, one non-blocking verify item (stdin envelope smoke-test deferred into TASK-051). PASS.
NOTE surfaced to human: 'no extra cost' carries an asterisk — headless -p draws from a separate monthly Agent-SDK credit pool (subscription, no API key, claim-once). Flagged for the human's awareness; not a technical blocker.
